discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators (the quantum spin Hall effect)
subfield: Condensed matter physics: topological phases of matter
motivation: In 2005 Kane and Mele showed that spin-orbit coupling can turn an ordinary insulator into a new phase protected by time-reversal symmetry, the quantum spin Hall state. They identified a Z2 topological invariant that separates it from trivial insulators, and they showed that it forces helical edge states that cannot be removed. This was an unexpected extension of band topology beyond the quantum Hall effect, and it needs no magnetic field. In 2007 Molenkamp's group gave the decisive confirmation. They measured quantized edge conductance in HgTe quantum wells, which Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang had proposed. The Z2 idea was soon extended to three-dimensional topological insulators, which have been observed in many materials. This work created the modern field of symmetry-protected topological matter. It changed how we classify insulators and superconductors, and it underlies current searches for Majorana modes and topological devices.
